SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.76
EXPLANATION: Strong aromatic ring bands at 1608 and 1003 cm⁻¹ indicate a benzene ring; the single, strong out-of-plane C–H bend near 818–805 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of para-disubstitution. A prominent C=O stretch at 1682 cm⁻¹ matches a conjugated aryl ketone (acetophenone-type) better than an aldehyde (which would also show weak aldehydic C–H stretches near 2720–2830 cm⁻¹, not observed). Methyl group signatures are present (CH stretches at ~2929 cm⁻¹, CH₃ deformation around 1382 cm⁻¹, and rocking near 956 cm⁻¹). These features collectively fit p-methylacetophenone (candidate 2) over the aldehyde or heteroaromatic alternatives.
